name: Spinal Epidural Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Definitive visualization of epidural arteriovenous malformation on spinal angiography or MRI with contrast
Presence of progressive myelopathy symptoms consistent with spinal cord compression or ischemia
Exclusion of other spinal vascular malformations such as dural arteriovenous fistula or intramedullary AVM
History of episodic radicular pain or neurological deficits correlating with lesion location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Definitive imaging confirmation plus clinical neurological signs consistent with spinal cord involvement, with exclusion of other vascular lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosis.

searchTerms: gradual stiffness and weakness in legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Epidural venous engorgement causing spinal cord compression
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure from swollen veins

common.symptomName: Radicular neuropathic pain localized to affected spinal segments
Sensory disturbances including paresthesia and hypoesthesia
searchTerms: abnormal sensations like pins and needles

common.symptomName: Bladder and bowel dysfunction due to spinal cord involvement
searchTerms: loss of bladder and bowel control
spinal cord causing bladder and bowel problems

common.symptomName: Lower limb weakness with gait instability
searchTerms: lower limb weakness with balance issues
difficulty walking due to weak legs

occasional.symptomName: Back pain localized to the affected spinal level
searchTerms: back pain at specific spine level

occasional.symptomName: Intermittent claudication-like symptoms in lower limbs

rare.symptomName: Paralytic episodes triggered by Valsalva maneuvers

laboratory: CSF analysis may show mild protein elevation without pleocytosis
imaging: Spinal MRI with contrast showing epidural vascular mass and cord compression
Spinal digital subtraction angiography demonstrating arteriovenous shunting in epidural space
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; typically sporadic
other: Electrophysiological studies may show delayed somatosensory evoked potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Dural AVF typically located intradural with different angiographic pattern
Different clinical progression and response to treatment
Located within spinal cord parenchyma rather than epidural space
More likely to cause intramedullary hemorrhage

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe radicular pain with neurological deficit
Signs of spinal cord hemorrhage or acute cord compression
